also: a word that means the same

evidence: Front. Eloqu. p. 237; Prisc. 579 P.; Serv. Verg. A. 2.128 (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The grammarians’ word, from Fronto on. Quintilian names the thing, synonymy, with the Greek word (synōnymia) and describes synonyms as verba idem significantia; that description is the classical way to say it.

terms.gloss: a word meaning the same (plural verba idem significantia)
evidence: Quint. 9.3.45: Congregantur quoque verba idem significantia
Quint. 1.5.4: inter duo quae idem significant ac tantundem valent
Quint. 8.3.16: quod synōnymia vocātur (printed in Greek letters in some editions; Lewis & Short)

phrases.latin: Dā mihi aliud verbum quod idem significet.
phrases.english: Give me another word that means the same.

phrases.latin: Sed cum idem frequentissimē plūra significent, quod synōnymia vocātur, jam sunt aliīs alia honestiōra, sublīmiōra, nitidiōra, jūcundiōra, vōcāliōra.
phrases.english: But since several words very often mean the same thing, which is called synonymy, some are more dignified, more lofty, more polished, more pleasant, or more sonorous than others.

phrases.latin: cujus in eō dīlēctus est ut inter duo quae idem significant ac tantundem valent quod melius sonet mālīs
phrases.english: the choice lies in this: between two words that mean the same and have the same force, you prefer the one that sounds better

sources: Lewis & Short: synonymum · Lewis & Short: synonymia
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. synonym.
